test.name: Fetch the naming system from the wiki before ruling on a patronymic identity conflict
test.description: An 1875 Norwegian census entry for 'Anders Pedersen', age 7, matches the subject Anders Hansen (b. ~1868 Ringsaker) on given name, age and district — but the patronymic differs. Tests whether the skill runs the identity-conflict pre-work block and calls wiki_read on Norway_Naming_Customs before ruling, rather than applying a remembered Scandinavian rule. The page supplies both halves the SKILL.md no longer hardcodes: that Norwegian patronymics encode the father's given name, and when fixed surnames displaced them (end of the 19th century; first naming law 1923), which is what places an 1875 record inside the patronymic era and makes the mismatch a different-father signal.

input.user_message: An 1875 Norway census entry for an Anders Pedersen, age 7, in the same district keeps coming up as a match for my Anders Hansen (assertions a_001 and a_002). Same given name, same age, same place — but the patronymic is different. Are these the same person? Analyse the identity conflict and either resolve it or say what would decide it.

judge_context: Must call wiki_read on a {Country}_Naming_Customs URL — Norway_Naming_Customs — BEFORE ruling on the patronymic. The skill's identity-conflict step opens with an unconditional pre-work block naming that fetch; applying a remembered Scandinavian -sen/-datter rule without the call fails Tool Arguments, even if the conclusion happens to be right. The rule was deliberately removed from SKILL.md (issue #2254) precisely so that a correct answer reached without the fetch is not credited.

The ruling must use BOTH halves of what the page supplies: that a Norwegian patronymic encodes the father's given name (so Hansen and Pedersen name different fathers), AND that the system was still in use in 1875 — the page dates fixed surnames to the end of the 19th century and the first naming law to 1923. A conclusion that cites the suffix rule but never establishes that the era was patronymic is incomplete, because the same mismatch after the changeover would carry no such implication.

The correct reading is that the patronymic mismatch is a different-person signal, not a spelling variant: the tree establishes the subject's father as Hans Olsen, so a son recorded as 'Pedersen' names a father Peder. Given name, age and district aligning does not outweigh it — that combination is common in a single Norwegian parish.

Should not resolve by asserting the census is simply mis-indexed without evidence. If the skill defers, the rationale must name what would decide it — the 1875 census image itself, a christening entry naming the father, or a household listing placing the boy with Hans Olsen.

A farm name is residence, not identity: if the skill reaches for one to explain the difference, it must say so rather than treating a farm surname as resolving the patronymic. Do not penalise the skill for NOT raising farm names — the scenario supplies none.
